newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Baht sinks after BOT announces managed float.
newsitem.headline: Baht sinks after BOT announces managed float.

text.p: The Thai currency sank nearly three baht against the U.S. dollar in immediate reaction to a surprise announcement from the Bank of Thailand that it intended a "managed float" of the beleagured currency.
The central bank said exchange rate movements were seen large at the initial stage of the managed float and that it will intervene in the forex market from time-to-time.
The offshore baht was quoted at 27.000/28.000 compared with around 24.25 just ahead of the announcement.

"The Thai exchange rate system from July 2, 1997 will be a managed float whereby the value of the baht will be determined by market forces to reflect fundamental economic forces," said Thailand's new Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya.
The market read the initial announcement that from now on the value of the baht would be "set by market forces" as a devaluation announcement.
But later the words "managed float" hit the newswires.
"It simply means they can stand away from intervening if they want to," said Chiang Yao Chye, economist at CIBC Wood Gundy. "It means they don't have to follow the four satang band any more."
In later trading the offshore baht slipped a little further against the dollar to 27.300/28.300.
